# Code of conduct

PugPort adopts the [Contributor Covenant, version 3.0](https://www.contributor-covenant.org/version/3/0/code_of_conduct/) as its code of conduct. The linked text is the standard. This page adds how it applies here: where it applies, how to report a problem, and who enforces it.

## In short

Be respectful and constructive. Welcome newcomers, accept that people write in English or Chinese, and criticize work, not people. Harassment, insults, sexualized language or imagery, personal or political attacks, and publishing someone else's private information are not acceptable here.

## Where it applies

This code applies in the PugPort repository (issues, pull requests, reviews, commit messages, and comments), in [GitHub Discussions](https://github.com/pugport/pugport/discussions), on the [PugPort Discord](https://discord.gg/2GsqpfHy55), and wherever someone represents PugPort in public. Text that an AI tool writes and you post counts as your own.

## Reporting

Report conduct concerns privately to a moderator on the [PugPort Discord](https://discord.gg/2GsqpfHy55), or through GitHub's **Report content** option. Do not report them in public issues.

Include links to the comments, issues, or pull requests involved. The owner keeps the reporter's identity private and shares report details only as far as needed to act on them. Security vulnerabilities follow [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) instead.

GitHub's **Report content** option works on any comment, issue, or pull request; those reports go to GitHub staff, not to the owner.

## Enforcement

The owner enforces this code and decides what to do about each report, following the Contributor Covenant's enforcement guidance: from a private warning up to a permanent ban from the repository, its discussions and the Discord server. Comments, commits, and pull requests that break this code can be edited, hidden, or closed.
